title: The Tokenized Treasury Interim Deployment's combined $5m allocation cap is not enforced by its per-Instance rate limits, which sum to twice that
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.14.1.2.5.1.1 and A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.14.2.2.5.1.1 state, identically, that "the maximum allocation for the Tokenized Treasury Basin Interim Deployments is **$5 million, combined across the JTRSY and BUIDL Instances**."

The rate limits do not implement that. A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.14.1.2.4.1 gives JTRSY an inflow `maxAmount` of 5,000,000 USDS with a 5,000,000 USDS per day slope, and .14.2.2.4.1 gives BUIDL exactly the same. Filling both to their on-chain limits produces $10 million of allocation while every enforced constraint is satisfied — the shared ceiling is breached without any limit being exceeded.

The Atlas elsewhere shows it knows how to close this gap. The Grove Diamond PAU Uniswap Instance registers an **Aggregate Deposit RateLimitID** with a "normalized" cap sitting above its per-asset limits, precisely so that spending across two legs cannot exceed one ceiling. No equivalent aggregate exists across JTRSY and BUIDL, even though the ceiling is explicitly written as a combined figure and both Instances point at the same Basin architecture.

So the $5 million cap is an operational constraint, honoured by whoever executes, not a coded one. Nothing on-chain prevents its breach, and the Instance documents do not name a monitoring process that would detect one — both Instances' *Instance-specific Operational Processes* sections (.14.1.3 and .14.2.3) are empty boilerplate.

This is the sharpest form of a general risk: where a mandate is expressed as an aggregate but enforcement is per-Instance, the number of Instances multiplies the real ceiling. The gap widens with every Instance added under the same combined cap.
description: JTRSY and BUIDL each carry a 5,000,000 USDS inflow limit while sharing a single $5 million combined ceiling; unlike the Diamond PAU Instance, no aggregate rate limit spans them.
